sections.history: Kuthalam, bearing the Tevaram name Tiruthuruthi, is an ancient Shaiva town near Mayiladuthurai on the road to Kumbakonam. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, sung by the three great Tevaram saints — Tirunavukkarasar (Appar), Tirugnana Sambandar and Sundarar — and is reckoned among the shrines on the southern bank of the Kaveri. The structural temple that stands today belongs to the Chola period and later, built in stone over the far older sacred site hymned by the saints.
sections.architecture: The temple is a modest delta shrine of Dravidian form, with the sanctum of Uthvedeeswarar, a Nandi, the goddess Amirtha Mughizhambikai in her own shrine, and the usual parivara devatas. The sthala vriksham is the Uddhala tree. A set of the lord's Padukas — sandals said to have been left here by Shiva — is venerated by devotees. The Manjalaru, a branch of the Kaveri, waters this part of the delta.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells of the sage Bharathama performing penance, from whose sacrificial fire the Goddess was born as a maiden. She worshipped a Shiva lingam set in the Kaveri, and the lord emerged from the linga and took her hand. From this grace the deity is praised as Uthvedeeswarar and the goddess as Amirtha Mughizhambikai. The name Sonnavararivar, 'he who knows what is spoken,' belongs to the lord's listening grace, and the revered Padukas mark his presence at this spot.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Panguni Uthiram in Panguni (March–April), and the Mondays of Karthikai, along with the regular Pradosha worship. These are observed at the quiet scale of a delta town shrine, drawing pilgrims who follow the Paadal Petra trail along the southern Kaveri.
sections.experience: A visit to Kuthalam joins the pilgrim to one of the lesser-trodden Tevaram shrines of the Kaveri's southern bank. Before Uthvedeeswarar and Amirtha Mughizhambikai, amid the memory of the goddess born of fire and the lord's own sandals, the devotee finds the unhurried devotion of a delta town that has kept its ancient hymns alive.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Kuthalam is about 9 km from Mayiladuthurai on the Mayiladuthurai–Kumbakonam road, roughly 1 km from the Kuthalam bus stand. Mayiladuthurai is the nearest major rail head, with frequent buses and taxis to Kuthalam.
